title: The ticket app on Eric's computers, restyled as a Japanese company's in-house system
caption: From your notes: "Maybe in day two, you get your first glimpse at the Windows 95 simple ticketing system with two tickets." and "You're paid per task." When the story sits Eric at his room PC or his B2 desk, the screen becomes that computer: a teal desktop, a grey Repair Tickets window with _ □ ×, a list with ID, Subject, From and Status, the ticket itself, a status bar and a taskbar with Start. Eric reads tickets and can take a new one. Closing one is always the story's, with no deadline and no penalty; when it closes he is paid what it says (¥3,000 and ¥5,000 for day 2's two), into the same yen as the drinks. The first time, a yellow tooltip says how to open one, then what Take does. Codex is putting the app into day 2 now (where it opens, and the hooks), so the build can't reach it yet; these shots run the same story steps in room 203 on day 2, and close T-0002 by hand to show the payment.

sections.title: After, Japanese in-house system: desktop, 1366 × 860
sections.caption: From your note: "I regret pure win 95, think japanese interfaces, corporate bad but simple design. Some japanese here, and learnable". The same app, now as Amakawa's in-house web tool: an address strip, a blue header with the red 天川 mark, a breadcrumb, thin-bordered zebra tables, coloured status badges, square buttons and a copyright line. Ten labels are in Japanese, each with its reading over it and the English after it: 件名, 依頼者, 状態, 未対応, 対応中, 完了, 報酬, 担当する, 戻る, 閉じる. Tapping a label, or using a button, puts the word in your Words; you never need one to play. Everything else works as before. Ticket subjects and texts are blurred in these shots.
